item.title: China-Singapore Maritime Cooperation-2026 Joint Exercise Kicks Off
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
ZHANJIANG, China, Sept. 5 -- The Chinese and Singaporean navies kicked off their "Maritime Cooperation-2026" joint exercise at a naval base in Zhanjiang City, South China's Guangdong Province, on September 5, 2026. The Chinese PLA Navy's Type 054A guided-missile frigate Dali (Hull 553) and the Republic of Singapore Navy's Formidable-class frigate RSS Steadfast (Hull 70) will participate in the exercise. The exercise will comprise a shore phase at a naval base from September 5 to 7, and a sea phase in waters off Zhanjiang City from September 8 to 9, 2026. During the shore phase, personnel from both navies will engage in planning exercises and professional exchanges. At sea, both navies will have an exchange of sea riders and conduct a range of serials. These include gunnery firings, communications and maneuvering exercises, as well as joint search and rescue and medical evacuation drills. Prior to this, China and Singapore have held four "Maritime Cooperation" joint naval exercises. In 2015, the two countries conducted their first bilateral naval exercise under the name "Maritime Cooperation-2015." Since then, the two navies have established a routine mechanism of alternating hosts, with the scale and influence of the exercises steadily growing.

item.title: China, Russia, Mongolia Hold Border Defense Cooperation 2026 Joint Exercise
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
By Du Juan, Zhang Tianye, Li Qingtong, Liu JInkui, Zhao Xiaolei, Zhang Wei, Chen Xiaodong, Li Zhenghua, Long Xitao, Li Pengru and Deng Siqi BEIJING, Sept. 5 -- The border defense troops dispatched by China, Russia and Mongolia conducted the Border Defense Cooperation 2026 joint exercise in a designated tri-border area located in Manzhouli, Inner Mongolia, China, from September 2 to 3, 2026. The joint exercise focused on "jointly preventing and combating reconnaissance and sabotage activities in border areas". The exercise was set against the scenario where terrorists escaped from Russian border area to the Chinese and Mongolian sides. During the exercise, the Russian troops dispatched helicopter to conduct air strike; the Mongolian troops blocked the escaping routes and the Chinese drone-assisted combat team detected and locked on the terrorists. Then, under the cover of FPV drones, an assault team advanced rapidly toward the terrorists’ hideout in armored all-terrain vehicles and stormed inside to arrest the terrorists. (Video Editor: Lin Congyi)

item.title: Xi urges greater efforts to nurture capable young people for socialist cause
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
BEIJING, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- Congratulating a popular national children's radio program on its 70th anniversary, Chinese President Xi Jinping urged professionals in children's culture to redouble efforts in nurturing a new generation of capable young people for the socialist cause. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the call in a congratulatory letter sent Friday to China Media Group's program named Xiaolaba, or Little Trumpet. He praised the program's 70-year commitment to "telling good stories to children," which have accompanied generations of young listeners as they grew up. Xi called on the program's team and professionals in children's culture to fulfill the mission of fostering virtue through education, keep pace with the times, tap deeply into the rich cultural resources, and devote themselves to creating more excellent and popular works that promote the true, the good and the beautiful among children. He urged greater efforts to nurture a new generation of capable young people with sound moral grounding, intellectual ability, physical vigor, aesthetic sensibility, and labor skills, who will be able to contribute to and carry forward the socialist cause. Launched on Sept. 4, 1956, Xiaolaba is the first radio program in the People's Republic of China dedicated to preschool children. It has since grown into a flagship program spanning radio, television, new media and in-school broadcasting.

item.title: China-Laos Peace Train 2026 Joint Humanitarian Medical Rescue Exercise to Be Held in Laos
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
BEIJING, Sept. 4 -- China-Laos Peace Train 2026 joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise will be held in Laos in September, said Senior Colonel Jiang Bin, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, on Friday. Taking international humanitarian medical rescue in a super typhoon disaster as its theme, the exercise focuses on such training subjects as joint on-site search and rescue, casualty evacuation, health and epidemic prevention, and psychological rescue. During the event, the Chinese side will also provide medical services for Lao military personnel and civilians. As the sixth exercise of this series, the joint exercise will further deepen and expand pragmatic exchange and cooperation in such fields as disaster medical rescue, tropical disease control and prevention, and infectious disease prevention and control, enhance the two militaries' capabilities in joint medical-service command, joint rescue, and joint prevention and control, and better provide quality public security goods for regional countries and peoples.

item.title: China urges Japanese authorities to make clean break with militarism to win trust: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Wednesday urged Japanese authorities to earnestly abide by the international obligations confirmed in the Japanese Instrument of Surrender, face up to history, make a clean break with militarism, and win the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community through concrete actions. Guo made the remarks at a regular media briefing when answering a question about China's position on the "Enemy State Clauses" in the UN Charter. On Sept. 2, 1945, the Japanese government formally signed the Instrument of Surrender and accepted all the provisions of the Potsdam Proclamation, confirming the nature of the war of aggression launched by Japanese militarism, he said. "This historical conclusion must not be tampered with, still less should the post-war international order be challenged," Guo said, adding that the "Enemy State Clauses" remain in the UN Charter to this day, and the relevant provisions, including Articles 53, 77 and 107, remain valid as well. Guo said these clauses constitute special institutional arrangements concerning the defeated countries of World War II, aim at preventing them from once again posing a threat to international peace and security, and provide important institutional safeguards for upholding the post-war international order. "Japan joined the UN on the premise that it acknowledged the crimes of militarism and accepted the UN Charter in its entirety," he added. Guo said that the Japanese authorities not only avoid addressing their historical responsibilities, but also pay homage to Class-A war criminals of World War II, distort and whitewash the crimes of aggression, accelerate remilitarization, seek to revise the pacifist Constitution, antagonize almost all of their neighboring countries, openly interfere in other countries' internal affairs, and even issue threats of force. "The 'gray rhino' of Japan's 'new militarism' is charging toward us, once again posing a threat to peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific. It is highly necessary to fully abide by the UN Charter and reaffirm the 'Enemy State Clauses,'" said Guo.
